methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $150M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Rondo Energy is a Series B climate and energy company founded by John O'Donnell and Eric Trusiewicz that has raised $150M+. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable (Linamar, ticker LNZA), with primary focus on three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage peers: KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C).

Two triangulation methods are applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $150M total raised as a value proxy and applies a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implying a valuation of $285M. Peer-median analysis derives a $1.0B valuation based on the three-company comparable set, which ranges from $700M to $3.0B. These methods reflect standard venture progression patterns and direct peer benchmarking within the climate and energy sector.

The triangulated analysis produces a low-to-high range of $242M to $1.1B, with a median of $642M. Key uncertainties include the limited peer sample size (n=3) and stage heterogeneity—all three comps are Series C, one stage ahead of Rondo. The 4.6x spread between low and high estimates reflects this gap and the volatility inherent in frontier climate tech valuations, where growth rates and exit multiples remain largely unproven.
